topic: Moser's Circle Problem: The Danger of Patterns
target_audience: Advanced High School Students / Early University Students

sections.title: The Setup: Connecting the Dots
lecture_lines: Place n points on a circle's circumference.
Connect every point to every other point.
How many regions do these lines create?
animations: Draw a white circle (#FFFFFF) and place two magenta points (#FF00FF) on it.
Connect points with a cyan line (#00FFFF), creating 2 regions.
Add a third point and connect to all others.
Add fourth point and connect, highlighting regions doubling.
Label regions sequentially as they increase to 8 in #FFFF00.

sections.title: The Seductive Pattern
lecture_lines: With 1 point, we have 1 region.
With 2 points, we get 2 regions.
With 3 points, the count reaches 4.
For 4 and 5 points, it's 8 and 16.
The pattern seems to double every time!
animations: Display a white table (#FFFFFF) with headers n and R.
Fill 'R' column with 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 for n=1-5.
Highlight the doubling pattern R = 2^(n-1) in green (#00FF00).

sections.title: The Great Betrayal (n=6)
lecture_lines: Let's test 6 points and expect 32 regions.
We carefully count every single slice.
Surprisingly, there are only 31 regions!
animations: Draw circle with 6 magenta points (#FF00FF) and all chords.
Sequentially number regions from 1 to 31 in white (#FFFFFF).
Pulse the total count '31' in red (#FF0000) to highlight discrepancy.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Euler's Planar Formula
lecture_lines: We treat the circle as a planar graph.
Euler's formula states V minus E plus F equals 2.
For regions, R equals E minus V plus 1.
animations: Write Euler's Formula V - E + F = 2 in yellow (#FFFF00).
Draw a triangle with labeled vertices, edges, and faces.
Derive R = E - V + 1 from the formula in white (#FFFFFF).

sections.title: Geometric Logic: Counting V and E
lecture_lines: Vertices include n boundary points and internal intersections.
Every 4 points create one internal intersection.
Total vertices V equals n plus nC4.
Edges connect vertices along chords and arcs.
Total edges E equals n plus nC2 plus 2nC4.
animations: Highlight 4 points on circle in magenta (#FF00FF).
Show chord intersection creating one internal vertex in cyan (#00FFFF).
Display V = n + nC4 in yellow (#FFFF00).
Display E = n + nC2 + 2(nC4) in cyan (#00FFFF).
Highlight how every 4 points create one internal intersection.

sections.title: The Final Formula
lecture_lines: Plug V and E into Euler's formula.
R equals E minus V plus 1.
R simplifies to nC4 plus nC2 plus 1.
For n=6, the formula gives 31 regions.
The doubling pattern was just a coincidence!
animations: Substitute V and E into R = E - V + 1 in white (#FFFFFF).
Simplify to R = nC4 + nC2 + 1 in yellow (#FFFF00).
Compute n=5 result as 16 in green (#00FF00).
Compute n=6 result as 31 in red (#FF0000).
Highlight why the powers of 2 pattern fails at n=6.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Lesson of Moser
lecture_lines: Patterns in math can be misleading.
Never rely on induction without a formal proof.
Always check the next case!
animations: Display 'Math requires rigorous proof' in white (#FFFFFF).
Show 'Induction can be misleading' in red (#FF0000).
Final view of Moser's formula nC4 + nC2 + 1.
